summary: @orieken/saturday-playwright-cesium gives Playwright tests a seam (window.__SATURDAY_CESIUM__ = { viewer, Cesium }) to act on a Cesium globe like a user and read back entities, screen projections and camera state without depending on pixels, following the same seam-contract pattern as @orieken/saturday-playwright-leaflet. The first developer-stage run was killed by the 30-minute stage timeout and finished by hand on branch salvage/saturday-playwright-cesium (commit 926ad56, not yet applied to this worktree); its own fixture suite (7 Vitest + 11 Playwright tests) covers all seven helpers (waitForSettled, getEntities, toScreen, clickAt, flyTo, metersPerPixelAt, globeRadiusMeters) and three radius-parameterized geometry functions (distance, lineLength, pointInCircle) against a static fixture globe named Aurelis (radius 6,000 km, baseLayerPicker/geocoder/ion off, local equirectangular image, no CDN). This order's job is to apply that salvage diff verbatim, verify every acceptance criterion against the real code rather than rewriting it, and resolve the one undecided structural question the salvage code already assumed an answer to: whether the geometry helpers stay package-local or move to a new packages/saturday-geo.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: An app under test exposes window.__SATURDAY_CESIUM__ = { viewer, Cesium } and attaches saturdayMetadata (id, name, kind) to each entity it wants tests to find, as documented in the package's own README seam contract.
examples: README.md section 1 shows (window as any).__SATURDAY_CESIUM__ = { viewer, Cesium } and entity.saturdayMetadata = { id, name, kind }
fixtures/assets/fixture-globe.js builds its own viewer and sets window.__SATURDAY_CESIUM__ after adding entities, proving the seam can attach asynchronously

acceptanceCriteria.statement: packages/saturday-playwright-cesium/fixtures/ serves a static page with a Cesium Viewer on a spherical ellipsoid of a declared radius, one equirectangular image covering the whole globe from the package's own files, baseLayerPicker/geocoder/ion imagery off, known point/line/circle entities carrying metadata, and makes no request off its own origin.
examples: fixtures/assets/fixture-globe.js: new Cesium.Ellipsoid(6_000_000, 6_000_000, 6_000_000); baseLayerPicker: false, geocoder: false; SingleTileImageryProvider.fromUrl('/assets/aurelis.jpg', ...)

Four saturdayMetadata-tagged entities (reagent-site-1 point, supply-route-1 line, exclusion-zone-1 circle, mystery-site-1 point with a deliberately unrecognized kind) plus one untagged point to prove exclusion
tests/fixture.spec.ts's 'fixture page makes no request off its own origin' test already asserts every http(s) request's hostname is 127.0.0.1

acceptanceCriteria.statement: cesium.waitForSettled() resolves once the globe's tiles are loaded, the camera has stopped, and no render is pending, and rejects with a message naming the stuck condition (tiles/camera/render/seam) after a timeout.
examples: fixture.ts's isSettled()/describeUnsettledConditions() check globe.tilesLoaded, a cameraMoving flag and a renderPending flag tracked via moveStart/moveEnd/postRender listeners
fixture.spec.ts already has one test asserting resolution and one forcing cameraMoving=true to assert the rejection message contains 'camera'

acceptanceCriteria.statement: cesium.getEntities() returns each saturdayMetadata-tagged entity's metadata and geometry in degrees and metres: point position, line endpoints, circle centre and radius.
examples: fixture.ts's extractEntities() dispatches on entity.ellipse/polyline/position, never on saturdayMetadata.kind, and excludes untagged entities
fixture.spec.ts asserts all four tagged entities' geometry, including the mystery-site-1 entity whose kind is 'unexpected-kind-value'

acceptanceCriteria.statement: cesium.toScreen(lat, lng) returns page coordinates, or null when the point is on the far side of the globe or off-screen.
examples: fixture.ts's projectToScreen() uses an EllipsoidalOccluder for far-side occlusion and a canvas-bounds check for off-screen, returning page (not canvas) coordinates via getBoundingClientRect()
fixture.spec.ts has one passing case, one far-side-null case, and one off-canvas-but-visible-null case

acceptanceCriteria.statement: cesium.clickAt(lat, lng) clicks through page.mouse, and a fixture test shows the globe's pick returned that location within the tolerance metersPerPixelAt gives.
examples: fixture.ts's clickAt() calls toScreen() then page.mouse.click(); throws if the point isn't visible
fixture.spec.ts installs a LEFT_CLICK pick handler and asserts the picked lat/lng is within metersPerPixelAt(lat,lng) * 2 metres of the requested point, for both a near-centre and a near-horizon case

acceptanceCriteria.statement: cesium.flyTo(lat, lng, heightMeters) moves the camera and waits until settled.
examples: fixture.ts's flyTo() calls camera.flyTo({ destination, duration: 0 }) then waitForSettled()
fixture.spec.ts asserts the camera's resulting lat/lng/height match the requested destination within tolerance

acceptanceCriteria.statement: distance, lineLength and point-in-circle checks take the globe's radius from the seam rather than assuming Earth's, and are unit-tested in Node without a browser; whether they live in this package or a shared saturday-geo is decided at the design gate.
examples: src/geometry.ts's distance/lineLength/pointInCircle all take an explicit radiusMeters/globeRadiusMeters parameter, zero Cesium or Playwright imports
tests/geometry.spec.ts runs under vitest (environment: node) and explicitly proves Earth's radius (6,371,000m) gives a different, wrong result than Aurelis's (6,000,000m)

geometry.ts's own header comment already asserts 'see architecture-notes.md's structural decision to keep this package-local' — but no architecture-notes.md exists for this feature yet, so the architect must ratify or override this, not treat it as already decided

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The package's test script runs the fixture suite in real Chrome (channel: 'chrome', headed, --use-gl=angle --use-angle=swiftshader) and passes with the literal AC9 docker command after dependencies are installed and the package is built; record its output in the delivery record.
examples: package.json's test script: 'vitest run && playwright test --project=chrome'

playwright.config.ts's 'chrome' project matches RUNNER_IMAGE_SOFTWARE_GL_ARGS = ['--use-gl=angle', '--use-angle=swiftshader'] literally, per docs/runner-image.md and the ui-suite-real-chrome precedent
docker run --rm --platform linux/amd64 --network none -v "$PWD:/work" saturday-runner:debian bash -lc 'cd /work && pnpm --filter @orieken/saturday-playwright-cesium test'

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Each helper's test fails when the fixture's corresponding value changes; for a helper reading nothing from the fixture, a change to the helper's own code that the test catches is the proof instead. Record, per helper, the change made and the failing output in the delivery record.
examples: metersPerPixelAt and globeRadiusMeters read nothing fixed from fixture-globe.js's entity list — their fail-proof must come from a deliberate code change (e.g. flipping camera.getPixelSize's args) rather than a fixture edit
waitForSettled/getEntities/toScreen/clickAt/flyTo each have a known fixture value (entity coordinates, circle radius, camera destination) that QA can perturb and revert

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The fixture's static server listens on 127.0.0.1 only.
examples: fixtures/serve.mjs: createServer(...).listen(port, '127.0.0.1', ...) — its own comment notes saturday-playwright-leaflet's serve.mjs omits the host argument (binding all interfaces) and that call must not be copied here

examples: scope.paths: packages/saturday-playwright-cesium/**, packages/saturday-geo/**, pnpm-lock.yaml, docs/features/saturday-playwright-cesium/**

edgeCases.case: metersPerPixelAt and globeRadiusMeters read no fixed value from fixture-globe.js's entity list
edgeCases.handling: Their fail-proof evidence per AC10 comes from a deliberate change to the helper's own code (e.g. swapping camera.getPixelSize's width/height arguments), not a fixture edit — document this distinction in the delivery record.

edgeCases.case: clickAt's pick tolerance must scale with ground resolution, not a fixed pixel/metre value
edgeCases.handling: Already handled: fixture.spec.ts computes tolerance as metersPerPixelAt(lat,lng) * 2 at both a near-centre and a near-horizon point.

edgeCases.case: toScreen must distinguish far-side occlusion from merely off-canvas
edgeCases.handling: Already handled: projectToScreen() checks EllipsoidalOccluder.isPointVisible() before the canvas-bounds check, with a dedicated test for each case.

edgeCases.case: waitForSettled must not resolve while the camera is still mid-move or a render is pending after it stops
edgeCases.handling: Already handled: moveStart/moveEnd/postRender listeners drive cameraMoving/renderPending flags; a dedicated test forces cameraMoving=true and asserts the rejection names 'camera'.

edgeCases.case: The seam may attach asynchronously (after an imagery provider resolves), not synchronously on page.goto()
edgeCases.handling: Already handled: pollUntilSettled() waits for window.__SATURDAY_CESIUM__ to exist before installing settle tracking, with its own named timeout message.

edgeCases.case: Applying the salvage diff via git apply --index may conflict if pnpm-lock.yaml has moved since 68a5901
edgeCases.handling: Developer verifies a clean apply and, on conflict, resolves by re-running pnpm install rather than hand-editing the lockfile.

edgeCases.case: The geometry.ts architecture decision is baked into four files before an architect has ratified it
edgeCases.handling: Architect stage must explicitly ratify or override before developer work proceeds; developer then updates all four citing comments to match the real decision.

Should distance/lineLength/pointInCircle move to a new packages/saturday-geo, or stay package-local as the salvage code's comments already assume? This is the architect's decision to make explicitly, not inherit from code written before architecture-notes.md existed.
